seeder:
     1	# Populates main's cache scope so PR runs warm-start from it. Saves the go
     2	# module, go build (incl. test compile), and golangci-lint caches.
     3	#
     4	# Caches are ref-scoped: PR runs read their own scope then fall back to the
     5	# base branch. Per .github/actions/go-cache/action.yml, PRs are restore-only,
     6	# so push-to-main is the only opportunity to populate the fallback scope.
     7	
     8	name: cache-seeder
     9	
    10	on:
    11	  push:
    12	    branches:
    13	      - main
    14	    paths:
    15	      - "go.sum"
    16	      - ".golangci.yml"
    17	      - ".github/actions/go-cache/action.yml"
    18	      - ".github/actions/go-setup/action.yml"
    19	      - ".github/workflows/cache-seeder.yml"
    20	
    21	concurrency:
    22	  group: cache-seeder
    23	  cancel-in-progress: true
    24	
    25	permissions:
    26	  contents: read
    27	
    28	jobs:
    29	  gobuild:
    30	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    31	    steps:
    32	      - uses: actions/checkout@9c091bb21b7c1c1d1991bb908d89e4e9dddfe3e0 # v7
    33	      - uses: ./.github/actions/go-setup
    34	      - run: make deps-backend deps-tools
    35	      - run: TAGS="bindata" make backend
    36	      - run: TAGS="bindata gogit" GOEXPERIMENT="" make backend
    37	      - name: warm test compile cache (bindata)
    38	        env:
    39	          TAGS: bindata
    40	          GOTEST_FLAGS: -race -list=^$$ -count=1
    41	        run: make test-backend
    42	      - name: warm test compile cache (bindata gogit)
    43	        env:
    44	          TAGS: bindata gogit
    45	          GOEXPERIMENT:
    46	          GOTEST_FLAGS: -race -list=^$$ -count=1
    47	        run: make test-backend
    48	      - name: warm integration compile cache

    50	          TAGS="bindata" make test-integration-compile
    51	          TAGS="bindata gogit" GOEXPERIMENT="" make test-integration-compile
    52	          TAGS="bindata gogit" GOTEST_FLAGS="-race" make test-integration-compile
    53	
    54	  lint:

    56	    strategy:

    58	      matrix:

gocache:
     1	name: go-caches
     2	description: Restore the go module, build, and golangci-lint caches. Save only on the cache-seeder workflow.
     3	
     4	# Only the cache-seeder workflow saves; rename requires updating cache-seeder.yml.
     5	# The lint job restores but does not save the gobuild cache, so only one writer
     6	# (the gobuild job) populates it and there is no contention on the cache key.
     7	# Seeder restores by exact key only (no restore-keys) so each go.sum seeds a clean
     8	# cache and size stays bounded; do not add restore-keys here. PR runs keep them.
     9	
    10	inputs:
    11	  lint-cache:
    12	    description: Restore (and save in cache-seeder) ~/.cache/golangci-lint
    13	    default: "false"
    14	
    15	runs:
    16	  using: composite
    17	  steps:
    18	    - if: ${{ github.workflow == 'cache-seeder' }}
    19	      uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
    20	      with:
    21	        path: ~/go/pkg/mod
    22	        key: gomod-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('go.sum') }}
    23	    - if: ${{ github.workflow != 'cache-seeder' }}
    24	      uses: actions/cache/restore@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
    25	      with:
    26	        path: ~/go/pkg/mod
    27	        key: gomod-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('go.sum') }}
    28	        restore-keys: gomod-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}
    29	    - if: ${{ github.workflow == 'cache-seeder' &amp;&amp; inputs.lint-cache != 'true' }}
    30	      uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
    31	      with:
    32	        path: ~/.cache/go-build
    33	        key: gobuild-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('go.sum') }}
    34	    - if: ${{ github.workflow != 'cache-seeder' || inputs.lint-cache == 'true' }}
    35	      uses: actions/cache/restore@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
    36	      with:
    37	        path: ~/.cache/go-build
    38	        key: gobuild-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('go.sum') }}
    39	        restore-keys: gobuild-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}
    40	    - if: ${{ inputs.lint-cache == 'true' &amp;&amp; github.workflow == 'cache-seeder' }}
    41	      uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
    42	      with:
    43	        path: ~/.cache/golangci-lint
    44	        key: golint-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('go.sum', '.golangci.yml') }}
    45	    - if: ${{ inputs.lint-cache == 'true' &amp;&amp; github.workflow != 'cache-seeder' }}
    46	      uses: actions/cache/restore@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
    47	      with:
    48	        path: ~/.cache/golangci-lint
    49	        key: golint-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('go.sum', '.golangci.yml') }}
    50	        restore-keys: golint-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}

snap:
# This approach highly depends on the "main" branch's push.

# To debug the logic:
# * last_committed_tag=v1.26.1 last_released_tag=v1.26.0 ./snap/part-gitea-pull.sh
#   it will checkout tag v1.26.1, and build that for "stable"
# * last_committed_tag=v1.26.1 last_released_tag=v1.26.1 recent_tag=v1.27.0-dev-205 ./snap/part-gitea-pull.sh
#   it will still use the current branch, and build it for "devel"

[ -z "$last_committed_tag" ] &amp;&amp; last_committed_tag="$(git for-each-ref --sort=taggerdate --format '%(tag)' refs/tags | tail -n 1)"
[ -z "$last_released_tag" ] &amp;&amp; last_released_tag="$(snap info gitea | awk '$1 == "latest/candidate:" { print $2 }')"

if [ "${last_committed_tag}" != "${last_released_tag}" ]; then
  # if the latest tag has not been released to stable, build that tag instead of default branch.
  echo "Build last committed tag ${last_committed_tag} for new release, fetching and checking out ..."
  git fetch --quiet
  git checkout --quiet "${last_committed_tag}"

shard:
name: pgsql-shard
description: Run one pgsql integration test shard

inputs:
  shard:
    description: Shard index
    required: true
  total-shards:
    description: Total shard count
    required: true
  run-migration:
    description: Also run migration tests
    default: "false"

runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
    - name: Add hosts to /etc/hosts
      shell: bash
      run: '[ -e "/.dockerenv" ] || [ -e "/run/.containerenv" ] || echo "127.0.0.1 pgsql ldap minio" | sudo tee -a /etc/hosts'
    - shell: bash
      run: make deps-backend
    - shell: bash
      run: make backend
      env:
        TAGS: bindata
    - name: run migration tests
      if: ${{ inputs.run-migration == 'true' }}
      shell: bash
      run: GITEA_TEST_DATABASE=pgsql make test-migration
    - name: run tests
      shell: bash
      run: GITEA_TEST_DATABASE=pgsql make test-integration
      env:
        # pgsql is chosen to be the unlucky one to run with the slow "race detector", it is about 60% slower.
        GOTEST_FLAGS: -race -timeout=40m
        TAGS: bindata gogit
        TEST_LDAP: 1
        TEST_SHARD: ${{ inputs.shard }}
        TEST_TOTAL_SHARDS: ${{ inputs.total-shards }}

## Problem

`main`'s CI status means nothing, `main` skips most of the test suites, and backend PRs are slow for a reason we can fix.

### Main is red on every push, so real failures go unnoticed

- `release-nightly-snapcraft` has failed or been cancelled on all 99 of its runs since the fork (78 failed, 21 cancelled, 0 passed). The latest one, [run 43539275792](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/43539275792), stops with `fatal: empty string is not a valid pathspec`. `snap/part-gitea-pull.sh:33` reads the newest tag with `%(tag)`, which is empty for lightweight tags, and all our `v1.27.3-csci435-*` tags are lightweight. Even with annotated tags it would fail at publish, because the repo has no Snap Store credentials and the `gitea` snap name belongs to upstream.
- `release-nightly` has never finished: 98 runs were cancelled and 1 is queued ([example](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/43537000589)). Its jobs need upstream's private `namespace-profile-gitea-release-*` runners. The next push cancels each run, or GitHub drops it after 24 hours in the queue.
- `release-tag-version` matches `v1.*`, so it has run for every sprint tag, and all three runs were cancelled after sitting queued for those runners: s0 ([35251424595](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/35251424595)), s1 ([37872246874](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/37872246874)) and s2 ([40956082407](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/40956082407)). The s3 tag will do the same.
- The noise is hiding a real failure. `db-tests` failed on `main` after two docs-only merges ([43345969430](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/43345969430), [43296442804](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/43296442804)) with the flaky `repo-issue-edit.test.ts` test from #171. Nobody noticed, because every `main` commit was already red.

### Main never runs most of the test suites

Every integration job in `pull-db-tests.yml` has `if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'` (lines 20, 56, 91, 188, 236), and `pull-e2e-tests.yml` runs only on pull requests too. A push to `main` runs `test-unit` and `sonarqube` (Go unit tests and Vitest coverage) and nothing else. Since PRs don't have to be up to date with `main` before merging, two PRs that each pass can break `main` together, and no integration or e2e run would show it. The Sprint 2 tag `v1.27.3-csci435-s2` (`40e0aa79`) has no test runs at all, so D8's Suite health section has no CI baseline to quote.

### Backend PRs take about 28 minutes, mostly compiling and waiting

Full backend `db-tests` runs take 23.3 to 30.1 min, with a median of about 27.6 (e.g. [43524265133](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/43524265133)). Waiting for a runner isn't the cause: the median wait is 2 seconds. The time goes to three things:

- The build cache is stale. `cache-seeder` has run once ([40807939468](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/40807939468), Oct 29), because it only triggers when `go.sum`, `.golangci.yml` or the cache files change. Its `gobuild-<go.sum hash>` key can never be overwritten, so the cache is now 141 commits behind `main`. It also warms the `-race` build but not `-race -cover`. As a result, each `test-unit` pass spends about 3.6 minutes compiling before the first package result, and every other Go test job compiles more than it should too.
- The two unit-test passes run one after the other. `test-unit` runs the normal pass (9.6 to 12.1 min) and then the `gogit` pass (9.4 to 11.5 min).
- `sonarqube` waits on `test-unit`. It has `needs: test-unit` and runs the Vitest coverage itself, so it can't start until both unit passes are done.

## Goal

`main` is green unless one of our own suites failed, it runs the integration and e2e suites after every merge and on every sprint tag, and anyone can run them against any ref. Backend PRs get the same checks as now, every database included, in noticeably less time.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: Given a push to `main` or a pushed `v1.*` tag, when CI runs, then `release-nightly`, `release-nightly-snapcraft`, `release-tag-version` and `release-tag-rc` show as skipped (not failed, cancelled or queued), and each skip condition has a same-line comment citing #181 and saying the workflow only runs upstream.
- [ ] AC2: Given a merge to `main`, when CI runs, then sqlite, MySQL, MSSQL and Postgres migration plus integration tests, Go unit tests, Vitest and the Playwright e2e suite all run against the merged commit. A newer merge never cancels a run that has already started.
- [ ] AC3: Given a team member opens Actions → `db-tests` or `e2e-tests` → Run workflow and enters a ref (e.g. `v1.27.3-csci435-s2`), or someone pushes a `v*-csci435-*` tag, when the run finishes, then the suites from AC2 have run against that ref.
- [ ] AC4: Given a push to `main`, when CI runs, then the Go build cache is saved again under a key tied to that commit and includes the `-race -cover` build. Given a backend PR opened after that, when `test-unit`'s normal pass runs, then the first package result appears at most 1 minute after `make test-backend` starts (about 3.6 minutes now).
- [ ] AC5: Given a backend PR, when `db-tests` runs, then the normal and `gogit` unit-test passes run as two separate jobs at the same time. Both run `make test-check`, and only the normal pass uploads Go coverage.
- [ ] AC6: Given any `db-tests` run, when it runs, then Vitest coverage runs in its own job, at the same time as the Go unit tests. `sonarqube` scans both coverage reports, and a failing Vitest test still makes the `db-tests` run fail. `sonarqube` runs only on pull requests and pushes to `main`, and is skipped on tag pushes and manual runs, so an old ref never replaces `main`'s analysis in SonarQube Cloud.
- [ ] AC7: Given four backend PR runs after the fix, when they finish, then the median wall-clock time of `db-tests` (from the run being created to its last job finishing, runner queue time included) is at most 20 minutes (about 27.6 now), and every job that ran on a backend PR before this change still runs. No database, `-race` or `gogit` coverage is removed.
- [ ] AC8: Given `pull-db-tests.yml`, `pull-e2e-tests.yml` and `pull-compliance.yml`, then every job in them has a job-level `timeout-minutes`, so a hung job stops there instead of at GitHub's 6-hour default.

## Out of Scope

- Fixing the flaky `repo-issue-edit.test.ts` test. That's #171. This issue makes sure such a failure turns `main` red where people will see it.
- The Postgres-only failures in `TestMilestoneBurndown/RealLifecycle` ([38276920412](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/38276920412) and two other branches) and `TestRepoCalendar` ([42658314475](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/42658314475)). They need their own bug report.
- Making status checks required, and protecting tags with a ruleset. Both need repo-admin rights. I'll propose them to the TA once AC2 is green, with one combined check job as the required check, because a skipped job counts as passing.
- Writing each suite's pass/fail/skip counts to the job summary, speeding up `lint-backend` (11 to 12 min, runs alongside the tests), and making individual integration tests faster (#37).

## Open Questions

- Is a 20-minute median (AC7) the right target? The next slowest jobs are MySQL and Postgres shard 1, at about 17 to 24 min on current runs, which still use the stale cache (26.0 and 22.4 min in [43524265133](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/43524265133)). The cache fix should shorten them, but by how much isn't measured yet. Getting below that means splitting those into more shards, which runs more jobs at once against the org's limit of 20.

## Evidence of Fix

Broken or missing CI check: links to runs before and after.
- **Before:** the runs linked under Problem, and the backend `db-tests` times (median about 27.6 min) with the compile time from [43524265133](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/43524265133).
- **After:**
  - the first push to `main` after the merge, with release workflows skipped (AC1), every suite run (AC2) and the cache saved (AC4);
  - the s3 tag push, with `release-tag-version` skipped and the suites run;
  - a manual run against `v1.27.3-csci435-s2` (AC3);
  - four backend PR runs with their times, their median and each job's compile time (AC4 to AC7);
  - the diff showing a job-level `timeout-minutes` on every job in the three files (AC8).

## Design Decision

### Decision 1: stopping the upstream release workflows

**Decision:** Add `if: github.repository == 'go-gitea/gitea'` to each job in the four release workflows, the same guard upstream already uses in `cron-*.yml` and `giteabot.yml`.
**Alternatives Considered:**
- *Fix the release workflows to work on the fork* (annotated tags, our own runners and store accounts). The team doesn't publish binaries, images or snaps, so this would be work for nothing.
- *Delete the files, or turn them off with `gh workflow disable`.* Deleting conflicts with upstream syncs. Turning them off can't be reviewed, only shows in the settings page, and is the kind of quiet silencing the course counts as small at most.
**Rationale:** These workflows publish upstream's builds and can't run here. The guard is upstream's own pattern, it goes through review in the diff, and a code comment records why.
**Consequences:** Their runs still appear in the Actions tab, marked skipped. If the team ever publishes its own builds, the guard has to come off.

### Decision 2: cutting backend PR time

**Decision:** Refresh the build cache on every push to `main`, run the two unit-test passes as parallel jobs, and move Vitest coverage out of the `test-unit` → `sonarqube` chain. Every database job still runs on every backend PR.
**Alternatives Considered:**
- *Run MySQL, MSSQL and Postgres on a PR only when it touches `models/`, `modules/setting/` or `services/migrations/`.* Rejected because the Postgres-only failures in `TestMilestoneBurndown` (three branches) and `TestRepoCalendar` came from `services/issue` and `routers/`, outside those paths, so they would have reached `main` without any warning.
- *Drop `-race` or the `gogit` pass on PRs.* That would save the most time, but it removes checks without fixing anything, and the course counts that as silencing.
- *Only add more shards.* It uses more runners for the same work, so PRs would start waiting on each other because of the org's limit of 20 jobs at once.
**Rationale:** Most of the extra time goes to compiling and to jobs waiting on each other. Fixing that shortens the run and keeps every check.
**Consequences:** One more job per backend PR. Each unit-test job sets up its own service containers. The 20-minute target is limited by the slowest database job.

### Decision 3: how the cache gets refreshed

**Decision:** `cache-seeder` runs on every push to `main`. It saves under `gobuild-<go.sum hash>-<commit sha>` with a `restore-keys` fallback to the newest entry, and warms `-race -cover` as well as `-race`. Update the comment at `.github/actions/go-cache/action.yml:7-8` to give the new reason.
**Alternatives Considered:**
- *Keep the key based only on `go.sum`.* A saved key can't be overwritten, so the cache never updates until `go.sum` changes.
- *Let PR jobs save the cache.* A PR's cache is only visible to that PR and the PRs based on it, so other PRs can't use it, and several jobs writing at once would fight over the same key.
**Rationale:** Caches saved from `main` are visible to every PR, and one key per commit means the newest build is always available.
**Consequences:** Each entry is about 2.25 GB against the repo's 10 GB cache limit, so GitHub keeps about four and evicts the oldest. The `gomod` and `golint` caches share that limit, so eviction can drop them too and slow `lint-backend` and module downloads. One extra seeder run per merge.

### Decision 4: running the suites on `main` and on demand

**Decision:** Let the existing `pull-db-tests.yml` and `pull-e2e-tests.yml` jobs run on `push` to `main`, on `v*-csci435-*` tags and on `workflow_dispatch` (with a `ref` input that checkout uses), by changing each `pull_request`-only condition to `github.event_name != 'pull_request' || <the existing files-changed check>`. The concurrency group for push runs is shared and `cancel-in-progress` is false, so a running job is never cancelled.
**Alternatives Considered:**
- *A new `main-suites.yml` that copies the jobs.* The copies would drift away from the PR jobs.
- *Turn the jobs into one `workflow_call` workflow used by both.* No copies, but it rewrites upstream's files the most, which makes upstream syncs harder.
**Rationale:** Changing the conditions keeps one definition for each job and touches as few upstream lines as possible. Starting a run by hand with a `ref` input works for old tags, which don't have this workflow file.
**Consequences:** About 9 jobs per merge on `main`. When merges come in bursts, a waiting run is replaced by the newest one, so a failure may cover more than one merge; that saves runner time against the org's limit of 20 jobs. Every suite still `needs: files-changed`, so on push, tag and manual runs that job has to succeed (or be bypassed) even when it has no base to compare against, or every suite is skipped.

## Scope

medium, `scope: medium`. Changes `pull-db-tests.yml`, `pull-e2e-tests.yml`, `pull-compliance.yml` (timeouts), `cache-seeder.yml`, the `go-cache` action and the four release workflows. No product code changes. Evidence needs several pushes to `main`, a tag push, a manual run against a tag and four timed PR runs, each checked against the before numbers.

- [ ] AC7: Given the first attempt of four backend PR runs after the fix (a backend PR is one where `files-changed` reports `backend == 'true'`; re-runs don't count), when they finish, then the median wall-clock time of `db-tests` (from the run being created to its last job finishing, runner queue time included) is at most 20 minutes (about 27.6 now), and every job that ran on a backend PR before this change still runs. No database, `-race` or `gogit` coverage is removed.
- [ ] AC8: Given `pull-db-tests.yml`, `pull-e2e-tests.yml` and `pull-compliance.yml`, then every job with steps has a job-level `timeout-minutes` of at most 60, so a hung job stops there instead of at GitHub's 6-hour default. The `files-changed` jobs are exempt: they call a reusable workflow, where GitHub doesn't allow `timeout-minutes`, and its `detect` job already has a 3-minute timeout.

## Out of Scope

- Fixing the flaky `repo-issue-edit.test.ts` test. That's #171. This issue makes sure such a failure turns `main` red where people will see it.
- The Postgres-only failures in `TestMilestoneBurndown/RealLifecycle` ([38276920412](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/38276920412) and two other branches) and `TestRepoCalendar` ([42658314475](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/42658314475)). They need their own bug report.
- Making status checks required, and protecting tags with a ruleset. Both need repo-admin rights. I'll propose them to the TA once AC2 is green, with one combined check job as the required check, because a skipped job counts as passing.
- Writing each suite's pass/fail/skip counts to the job summary, speeding up `lint-backend` (11 to 12 min, runs alongside the tests), and making individual integration tests faster (#37).

## Open Questions

- Is a 20-minute median (AC7) the right target? The next slowest jobs are MySQL and Postgres shard 1, at about 17 to 24 min on current runs, which still use the stale cache (26.0 and 22.4 min in [43524265133](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/43524265133)). The cache fix should shorten them, but by how much isn't measured yet. Getting below that means splitting those into more shards, which runs more jobs at once against the org's limit of 20. This has to be settled before coding starts: either adding a shard to the slowest database job is in scope when the cache fix alone doesn't reach 20 minutes, or the target is raised to what the cache fix measures.

- **Before:** the runs linked under Problem, and the backend `db-tests` times (median about 27.6 min) with the compile time from [43524265133](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/43524265133).
- **After:**
  - the first push to `main` after the merge, with release workflows skipped (AC1), every suite run (AC2) and the cache saved (AC4);
  - a manual run against `v1.27.3-csci435-s2` (AC3);
  - four backend PR runs with their times, their median and each job's compile time (AC4 to AC7);
  - the diff showing a job-level `timeout-minutes` on every job in the three files (AC8).

Every After item needs the change on `main`, so the PR's Test Evidence lists them as manual, post-merge checks, and the results go in a comment on this issue. The s3 tag push (`release-tag-version` skipped, suites run) only happens at the D9 release, after this issue closes, so it gets a follow-up comment here and isn't part of the closing evidence.

## Design Decision

### Decision 1: stopping the upstream release workflows

**Decision:** Add `if: github.repository == 'go-gitea/gitea'` to each job in the four release workflows, the same guard upstream already uses in `cron-*.yml` and `giteabot.yml`.
**Alternatives Considered:**
- *Fix the release workflows to work on the fork* (annotated tags, our own runners and store accounts). The team doesn't publish binaries, images or snaps, so this would be work for nothing.
- *Delete the files, or turn them off with `gh workflow disable`.* Deleting conflicts with upstream syncs. Turning them off can't be reviewed, only shows in the settings page, and is the kind of quiet silencing the course counts as small at most.
**Rationale:** These workflows publish upstream's builds and can't run here. The guard is upstream's own pattern, it goes through review in the diff, and a code comment records why.
**Consequences:** Their runs still appear in the Actions tab, marked skipped. If the team ever publishes its own builds, the guard has to come off.

### Decision 2: cutting backend PR time

**Decision:** Refresh the build cache on every push to `main`, run the two unit-test passes as parallel jobs, and move Vitest coverage out of the `test-unit` → `sonarqube` chain. Every database job still runs on every backend PR.
**Alternatives Considered:**
- *Run MySQL, MSSQL and Postgres on a PR only when it touches `models/`, `modules/setting/` or `services/migrations/`.* Rejected because the Postgres-only failures in `TestMilestoneBurndown` (three branches) and `TestRepoCalendar` came from `services/issue` and `routers/`, outside those paths, so they would have reached `main` without any warning.
- *Drop `-race` or the `gogit` pass on PRs.* That would save the most time, but it removes checks without fixing anything, and the course counts that as silencing.
- *Only add more shards.* It uses more runners for the same work, so PRs would start waiting on each other because of the org's limit of 20 jobs at once.
**Rationale:** Most of the extra time goes to compiling and to jobs waiting on each other. Fixing that shortens the run and keeps every check.
**Consequences:** One more job per backend PR. Each unit-test job sets up its own service containers. The 20-minute target is limited by the slowest database job.

### Decision 3: how the cache gets refreshed

**Decision:** `cache-seeder` runs on every push to `main`. It saves under `gobuild-<go.sum hash>-<commit sha>` with a `restore-keys` fallback to the newest entry, and warms `-race -cover` as well as `-race`. Update the comment at `.github/actions/go-cache/action.yml:7-8` to give the new reason.
**Alternatives Considered:**
- *Keep the key based only on `go.sum`.* A saved key can't be overwritten, so the cache never updates until `go.sum` changes.
- *Let PR jobs save the cache.* A PR's cache is only visible to that PR and the PRs based on it, so other PRs can't use it, and several jobs writing at once would fight over the same key.
**Rationale:** Caches saved from `main` are visible to every PR, and one key per commit means the newest build is always available.
**Consequences:** Each entry is about 2.25 GB against the repo's 10 GB cache limit, so GitHub keeps about four and evicts the oldest. The `gomod` and `golint` caches share that limit, so eviction can drop them too and slow `lint-backend` and module downloads. One extra seeder run per merge.

### Decision 4: running the suites on `main` and on demand

**Decision:** Let the existing `pull-db-tests.yml` and `pull-e2e-tests.yml` jobs run on `push` to `main`, on `v*-csci435-*` tags and on `workflow_dispatch` (with a `ref` input that checkout uses), by changing each `pull_request`-only condition to `github.event_name != 'pull_request' || <the existing files-changed check>`. Pushes to `main` share one concurrency group with `cancel-in-progress` false, so a running job is never cancelled. Each tag and each manual run gets its own group, so it neither waits on nor replaces a `main` run. Pull request runs keep the group they have now.
**Alternatives Considered:**
- *A new `main-suites.yml` that copies the jobs.* The copies would drift away from the PR jobs.
- *Turn the jobs into one `workflow_call` workflow used by both.* No copies, but it rewrites upstream's files the most, which makes upstream syncs harder.
- *Keep the `files-changed` filter on pushes to `main`, so docs-only merges skip the suites.* Most merges here are docs-only, and the two `db-tests` failures linked under Problem both came after docs-only merges, so repeat runs on an unchanged tree are how a flaky test shows up. Replacing the waiting run caps the cost at one queued run.
**Rationale:** Changing the conditions keeps one definition for each job and touches as few upstream lines as possible. Starting a run by hand with a `ref` input works for old tags, which don't have this workflow file.
**Consequences:** About 9 jobs per merge on `main`. When merges come in bursts, a waiting run is replaced by the newest one, so a failure may cover more than one merge, and the replaced run shows as cancelled on its commit; that saves runner time against the org's limit of 20 jobs. Every suite still `needs: files-changed`, so on push, tag and manual runs that job has to succeed (or be bypassed) even when it has no base to compare against, or every suite is skipped. A manual run takes the workflow file from `main` but `.github/actions/*` and the Makefile from the ref it checks out. `v1.27.3-csci435-s2` has the same actions and make targets as `main`; a ref from before those existed may not run.

## Scope

medium, `scope: medium`. Changes `pull-db-tests.yml`, `pull-e2e-tests.yml`, `pull-compliance.yml` (timeouts), `cache-seeder.yml`, the `go-cache` action and the four release workflows. No product code changes. Evidence needs several pushes to `main`, a tag push, a manual run against a tag and four timed PR runs, each checked against the before numbers.

_**Agent (claude-fable-5-2 2026-11-14 02:36:00Z)**_

It's asking: **is "backend PR checks finish in 20 minutes" a promise you can actually keep?**

AC7 says the checks must drop from about 28 minutes to 20 or less. A CI run is only as fast as its slowest job, because the jobs run side by side and the run ends when the last one does. Your fixes speed up three things: the stale build cache, the two unit-test passes running back to back, and SonarQube waiting on them. After that, the slowest jobs left are the MySQL and Postgres integration tests, which take 17 to 24 minutes today.

The stale cache is part of why those are slow, so the cache fix should shorten them. Nobody has measured by how much. If they land at 16 minutes, you pass. If they land at 22, AC7 fails even though everything you built works.

So the question is what you commit to if the cache fix alone isn't enough:

- **Keep 20 minutes and add a shard.** Split the slowest database job into two jobs that each run half the tests. This will reach the target, but it is more work and puts more jobs in the queue at once, against the org's limit of 20 concurrent jobs.
- **Loosen the target.** Change AC7 to whatever the cache fix actually delivers, say 22 or 23 minutes. This is less work, but the number is then set by the result rather than chosen up front.

It has to be settled before coding because an acceptance criterion must be pass/fail. Left open, you could finish the work and still not know whether the issue is done.

_**Agent (claude-fable-5-2 2026-11-14 02:37:48Z)**_

Yes, two ways use only data that already exists, and a third is a throwaway experiment.

1. **Compare against the runs right after Oct 29.** The cache was seeded once that day, so backend PR runs in the next day or two had a nearly fresh cache. Their MySQL and Postgres job times against today's show roughly what a fresh cache buys. The catch is that the test suite has grown since, so the old numbers flatter the result a little.

2. **Split a current run into compile time and test time.** The job logs have timestamps, so for MySQL and Postgres shard 1 you can read how long passes before the first test result and how long the tests themselves take. A perfect cache can only remove the compile part. If the tests alone take more than about 18 minutes, 20 is out of reach without another shard, whatever the cache does.

3. **Run it for real on a scratch branch.** Open a draft PR whose only change lets the PR save its own build cache, run it once to fill the cache, then re-run and time it. This is the most accurate, but each cache entry is about 2.25 GB against the 10 GB limit, so it can evict `main`'s caches. It also costs two full CI runs.

I'd do 1 and 2 together: both are read-only `gh` queries, and 2 gives a hard floor while 1 gives a realistic estimate. Option 3 is only worth it if those two leave the answer close to 20. Say the word and I'll pull the numbers.

_**Agent (claude-fable-5-2 2026-11-14 02:41:03Z)**_

The 20-minute target is a coin flip with the cache fix alone: the projected median is 19.8 minutes, and 5 of 14 simulated runs land over 20.

**Fresh cache vs. stale cache (median minutes per job)**

| Job | Fresh (Oct 29, 2 runs) | Stale (Nov 11–13, 14 runs) | Compile part, stale → fresh | Tests alone, stale |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| MySQL | 16.6 | 20.6 | 4.2 → 0.9 | 11.9 |
| MSSQL | 15.3 | 21.7 | 3.9 → 0.8 | 12.3 |
| Postgres shard 1 | 14.7 | 21.4 | 6.8 → 1.3 | 11.1 |
| Postgres shard 2 | 15.2 | 17.3 | 4.6 → 0.9 | 9.4 |
| sqlite | 14.5 | 18.6 | 5.1 → 0.9 | 9.9 |

- **Whole run:** the two fresh-cache runs took 19.8 and 16.7 minutes; the 14 stale runs have a median of 28.8.
- **Unit tests:** the first package result came after 0.3 to 0.4 minutes with a fresh cache and 3.5 minutes now, so AC4's 1-minute bound is realistic. Those fresh runs predate `-cover`, so that part is untested.
- **Floor:** with zero compile time, MySQL and MSSQL still need about 16 to 17 minutes each (setup about 3, migrations about 1, tests about 12).

**Projection**

I took each of the 14 recent runs, swapped its compile time for the fresh-cache figure, and split the unit passes.

- **Database jobs are the limiter:** the slowest one finishes at a median of 19.8 minutes. It was MySQL in 7 runs, MSSQL in 5, and sqlite and Postgres shard 1 once each.
- **The unit chain is not:** unit tests plus SonarQube finish at 15 to 17.5 minutes.
- **Runner noise is large:** MySQL ranged from 16.5 to 27.2 minutes on the same stale cache, so four runs can easily miss a 20-minute median by luck.

**What this means for the spec**

- **One extra shard won't do it.** MySQL and MSSQL trade places as the slowest job, so you'd have to split both. That changes my earlier recommendation.
- **I'd set AC7 to 22 minutes instead.** 12 of the 14 simulated runs come in under 22, and it is still about 7 minutes faster than today.
- **AC6 saves almost nothing.** The Vitest step takes about 6 seconds and the whole `sonarqube` job about 3 minutes. The time saving comes from splitting the unit passes; moving Vitest only keeps its failures visible.
- **A cheaper lever exists if you want 20.** In the one MySQL log I read, `go-setup` spent about 70 seconds on `free-disk-space` and 55 seconds restoring caches. I haven't checked whether the disk cleanup is needed.

The fresh-cache sample is only two runs, because only two backend PRs ran within a day of the seeder. The suite has also grown slightly since, from about 720 to 729 integration tests.

Should I change AC7 to 22 minutes and replace the Open Question with these numbers?

## Problem

`main`'s CI status means nothing, `main` skips most of the test suites, and backend PRs are slow for a reason we can fix.

### Main is red on every push, so real failures go unnoticed

- `release-nightly-snapcraft` has failed or been cancelled on all 99 of its runs since the fork (78 failed, 21 cancelled, 0 passed). The latest one, [run 43539275792](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/43539275792), stops with `fatal: empty string is not a valid pathspec`. `snap/part-gitea-pull.sh:33` reads the newest tag with `%(tag)`, which is empty for lightweight tags, and all our `v1.27.3-csci435-*` tags are lightweight. Even with annotated tags it would fail at publish, because the repo has no Snap Store credentials and the `gitea` snap name belongs to upstream.
- `release-nightly` has never finished: 98 runs were cancelled and 1 is queued ([example](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/43537000589)). Its jobs need upstream's private `namespace-profile-gitea-release-*` runners. The next push cancels each run, or GitHub drops it after 24 hours in the queue.
- `release-tag-version` matches `v1.*`, so it has run for every sprint tag, and all three runs were cancelled after sitting queued for those runners: s0 ([35251424595](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/35251424595)), s1 ([37872246874](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/37872246874)) and s2 ([40956082407](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/40956082407)). The s3 tag will do the same.
- The noise is hiding a real failure. `db-tests` failed on `main` after two docs-only merges ([43345969430](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/43345969430), [43296442804](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/43296442804)) with the flaky `repo-issue-edit.test.ts` test from #171. Nobody noticed, because every `main` commit was already red.

### Main never runs most of the test suites

Every integration job in `pull-db-tests.yml` has `if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'` (lines 20, 56, 91, 188, 236), and `pull-e2e-tests.yml` runs only on pull requests too. A push to `main` runs `test-unit` and `sonarqube` (Go unit tests and Vitest coverage) and nothing else. Since PRs don't have to be up to date with `main` before merging, two PRs that each pass can break `main` together, and no integration or e2e run would show it. The Sprint 2 tag `v1.27.3-csci435-s2` (`40e0aa79`) has no test runs at all, so D8's Suite health section has no CI baseline to quote.

### Backend PRs take about 28 minutes, mostly compiling and waiting

Full backend `db-tests` runs take 23.3 to 30.1 min, with a median of about 27.6 (e.g. [43524265133](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/43524265133)). Waiting for a runner isn't the cause: the median wait is 2 seconds. The time goes to three things:

- The build cache is stale. `cache-seeder` has run once ([40807939468](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/40807939468), Oct 29), because it only triggers when `go.sum`, `.golangci.yml` or the cache files change. Its `gobuild-<go.sum hash>` key can never be overwritten, so the cache is now 141 commits behind `main`. It also warms the `-race` build but not `-race -cover`. As a result, each `test-unit` pass spends about 3.6 minutes compiling before the first package result, and every other Go test job compiles more than it should too.
- The two unit-test passes run one after the other. `test-unit` runs the normal pass (9.6 to 12.1 min) and then the `gogit` pass (9.4 to 11.5 min).
- `sonarqube` waits on `test-unit`. It has `needs: test-unit` and runs the Vitest coverage itself, so it can't start until both unit passes are done.

## Goal

`main` is green unless one of our own suites failed, it runs the integration and e2e suites after every merge and on every sprint tag, and anyone can run them against any ref. Backend PRs get the same checks as now, every database included, in noticeably less time.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: Given a push to `main`, when CI runs, then `release-nightly` and `release-nightly-snapcraft` show as skipped (not failed, cancelled or queued). Given a pushed `v1.*` tag, `release-tag-version` shows as skipped. `release-tag-rc` only triggers on `v1*-rc*` tags, which the course never pushes, so its guard is checked in the diff. Every job in the four workflows has the skip condition, with a same-line comment citing #181 and saying the workflow only runs upstream.
- [ ] AC2: Given any merge to `main`, docs-only ones included, when CI runs, then sqlite, MySQL, MSSQL and Postgres migration plus integration tests, Go unit tests, Vitest and the Playwright e2e suite all run against the merged commit. A newer merge never cancels a run that has already started. If several merges land while a run is in progress, only the newest waiting run is kept: the suites then run against the newest merged commit, and the replaced run shows as cancelled, never failed.
- [ ] AC3: Given a team member opens Actions → `db-tests` or `e2e-tests` → Run workflow and enters a ref (e.g. `v1.27.3-csci435-s2`), or someone pushes a `v*-csci435-*` tag, when the run finishes, then the suites from AC2 have run against that ref. A tag run or manual run never replaces a `main` run and is never replaced by one.
- [ ] AC4: Given a push to `main`, when CI runs, then the Go build cache is saved again under a key tied to that commit and includes the `-race -cover` build. Given a backend PR branched from `main` after that save, with no Go changes under `modules/` or `models/` (changes there recompile most of the tree whatever the cache holds), when `test-unit`'s normal pass runs, then the first package result appears at most 1 minute after `make test-backend` starts (about 3.6 minutes now).
- [ ] AC5: Given a backend PR, when `db-tests` runs, then the normal and `gogit` unit-test passes run as two separate jobs at the same time. Both run `make test-check`, and only the normal pass uploads Go coverage.
- [ ] AC6: Given any `db-tests` run, when it runs, then Vitest coverage runs in its own job, at the same time as the Go unit tests. `sonarqube` scans both coverage reports, and a failing Vitest test still makes the `db-tests` run fail. `sonarqube` runs only on pull requests and pushes to `main`, and is skipped on tag pushes and manual runs, so an old ref never replaces `main`'s analysis in SonarQube Cloud.
- [ ] AC7: Given the first attempt of four backend PR runs after the fix (a backend PR is one where `files-changed` reports `backend == 'true'`; re-runs don't count), when they finish, then the median wall-clock time of `db-tests` (from the run being created to its last job finishing, runner queue time included) is at most 20 minutes (about 27.6 now), and every job that ran on a backend PR before this change still runs. No database, `-race` or `gogit` coverage is removed.
- [ ] AC8: Given `pull-db-tests.yml`, `pull-e2e-tests.yml` and `pull-compliance.yml`, then every job with steps has a job-level `timeout-minutes` of at most 60, so a hung job stops there instead of at GitHub's 6-hour default. The `files-changed` jobs are exempt: they call a reusable workflow, where GitHub doesn't allow `timeout-minutes`, and its `detect` job already has a 3-minute timeout.

## Out of Scope

- Fixing the flaky `repo-issue-edit.test.ts` test. That's #171. This issue makes sure such a failure turns `main` red where people will see it.
- The Postgres-only failures in `TestMilestoneBurndown/RealLifecycle` ([38276920412](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/38276920412) and two other branches) and `TestRepoCalendar` ([42658314475](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/42658314475)). They need their own bug report.
- Making status checks required, and protecting tags with a ruleset. Both need repo-admin rights. I'll propose them to the TA once AC2 is green, with one combined check job as the required check, because a skipped job counts as passing.
- Writing each suite's pass/fail/skip counts to the job summary, speeding up `lint-backend` (11 to 12 min, runs alongside the tests), and making individual integration tests faster (#37).

## Open Questions

- Is a 20-minute median (AC7) the right target? The next slowest jobs are MySQL and Postgres shard 1, at about 17 to 24 min on current runs, which still use the stale cache (26.0 and 22.4 min in [43524265133](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/43524265133)). The cache fix should shorten them, but by how much isn't measured yet. Getting below that means splitting those into more shards, which runs more jobs at once against the org's limit of 20. This has to be settled before coding starts: either adding a shard to the slowest database job is in scope when the cache fix alone doesn't reach 20 minutes, or the target is raised to what the cache fix measures.

## Evidence of Fix

Broken or missing CI check: links to runs before and after.
- **Before:** the runs linked under Problem, and the backend `db-tests` times (median about 27.6 min) with the compile time from [43524265133](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/43524265133).
- **After:**
  - the first push to `main` after the merge, with release workflows skipped (AC1), every suite run (AC2) and the cache saved (AC4);
  - a manual run against `v1.27.3-csci435-s2` (AC3);
  - four backend PR runs with their times, their median and each job's compile time (AC4 to AC7);
  - the diff showing a job-level `timeout-minutes` on every job in the three files (AC8).

Every After item needs the change on `main`, so the PR's Test Evidence lists them as manual, post-merge checks, and the results go in a comment on this issue. The s3 tag push (`release-tag-version` skipped, suites run) only happens at the D9 release, after this issue closes, so it gets a follow-up comment here and isn't part of the closing evidence.

## Design Decision

### Decision 1: stopping the upstream release workflows

**Decision:** Add `if: github.repository == 'go-gitea/gitea'` to each job in the four release workflows, the same guard upstream already uses in `cron-*.yml` and `giteabot.yml`.
**Alternatives Considered:**
- *Fix the release workflows to work on the fork* (annotated tags, our own runners and store accounts). The team doesn't publish binaries, images or snaps, so this would be work for nothing.
- *Delete the files, or turn them off with `gh workflow disable`.* Deleting conflicts with upstream syncs. Turning them off can't be reviewed, only shows in the settings page, and is the kind of quiet silencing the course counts as small at most.
**Rationale:** These workflows publish upstream's builds and can't run here. The guard is upstream's own pattern, it goes through review in the diff, and a code comment records why.
**Consequences:** Their runs still appear in the Actions tab, marked skipped. If the team ever publishes its own builds, the guard has to come off.

### Decision 2: cutting backend PR time

**Decision:** Refresh the build cache on every push to `main`, run the two unit-test passes as parallel jobs, and move Vitest coverage out of the `test-unit` → `sonarqube` chain. Every database job still runs on every backend PR.
**Alternatives Considered:**
- *Run MySQL, MSSQL and Postgres on a PR only when it touches `models/`, `modules/setting/` or `services/migrations/`.* Rejected because the Postgres-only failures in `TestMilestoneBurndown` (three branches) and `TestRepoCalendar` came from `services/issue` and `routers/`, outside those paths, so they would have reached `main` without any warning.
- *Drop `-race` or the `gogit` pass on PRs.* That would save the most time, but it removes checks without fixing anything, and the course counts that as silencing.
- *Only add more shards.* It uses more runners for the same work, so PRs would start waiting on each other because of the org's limit of 20 jobs at once.
**Rationale:** Most of the extra time goes to compiling and to jobs waiting on each other. Fixing that shortens the run and keeps every check.
**Consequences:** One more job per backend PR. Each unit-test job sets up its own service containers. The 20-minute target is limited by the slowest database job.

### Decision 3: how the cache gets refreshed

**Decision:** `cache-seeder` runs on every push to `main`. It saves under `gobuild-<go.sum hash>-<commit sha>` with a `restore-keys` fallback to the newest entry, and warms `-race -cover` as well as `-race`. Update the comment at `.github/actions/go-cache/action.yml:7-8` to give the new reason.
**Alternatives Considered:**
- *Keep the key based only on `go.sum`.* A saved key can't be overwritten, so the cache never updates until `go.sum` changes.
- *Let PR jobs save the cache.* A PR's cache is only visible to that PR and the PRs based on it, so other PRs can't use it, and several jobs writing at once would fight over the same key.
**Rationale:** Caches saved from `main` are visible to every PR, and one key per commit means the newest build is always available.
**Consequences:** Each entry is about 2.25 GB against the repo's 10 GB cache limit, so GitHub keeps about four and evicts the oldest. The `gomod` and `golint` caches share that limit, so eviction can drop them too and slow `lint-backend` and module downloads. One extra seeder run per merge.

### Decision 4: running the suites on `main` and on demand

**Decision:** Let the existing `pull-db-tests.yml` and `pull-e2e-tests.yml` jobs run on `push` to `main`, on `v*-csci435-*` tags and on `workflow_dispatch` (with a `ref` input that checkout uses), by changing each `pull_request`-only condition to `github.event_name != 'pull_request' || <the existing files-changed check>`. Pushes to `main` share one concurrency group with `cancel-in-progress` false, so a running job is never cancelled. Each tag and each manual run gets its own group, so it neither waits on nor replaces a `main` run. Pull request runs keep the group they have now.
**Alternatives Considered:**
- *A new `main-suites.yml` that copies the jobs.* The copies would drift away from the PR jobs.
- *Turn the jobs into one `workflow_call` workflow used by both.* No copies, but it rewrites upstream's files the most, which makes upstream syncs harder.
- *Keep the `files-changed` filter on pushes to `main`, so docs-only merges skip the suites.* Most merges here are docs-only, and the two `db-tests` failures linked under Problem both came after docs-only merges, so repeat runs on an unchanged tree are how a flaky test shows up. Replacing the waiting run caps the cost at one queued run.
**Rationale:** Changing the conditions keeps one definition for each job and touches as few upstream lines as possible. Starting a run by hand with a `ref` input works for old tags, which don't have this workflow file.
**Consequences:** About 9 jobs per merge on `main`. When merges come in bursts, a waiting run is replaced by the newest one, so a failure may cover more than one merge, and the replaced run shows as cancelled on its commit; that saves runner time against the org's limit of 20 jobs. Every suite still `needs: files-changed`, so on push, tag and manual runs that job has to succeed (or be bypassed) even when it has no base to compare against, or every suite is skipped. A manual run takes the workflow file from `main` but `.github/actions/*` and the Makefile from the ref it checks out. `v1.27.3-csci435-s2` has the same actions and make targets as `main`; a ref from before those existed may not run.

## Scope

medium, `scope: medium`. Changes `pull-db-tests.yml`, `pull-e2e-tests.yml`, `pull-compliance.yml` (timeouts), `cache-seeder.yml`, the `go-cache` action and the four release workflows. No product code changes. Evidence needs several pushes to `main`, a tag push, a manual run against a tag and four timed PR runs, each checked against the before numbers.

**Decision:** Add `if: github.repository == 'go-gitea/gitea'` to each job in the four release workflows, the same guard upstream already uses in `cron-*.yml` and `giteabot.yml`.
**Alternatives Considered:**
- *Fix the release workflows to work on the fork* (annotated tags, our own runners and store accounts). The team doesn't publish binaries, images or snaps, so this would be work for nothing.
- *Delete the files, or turn them off with `gh workflow disable`.* Deleting conflicts with upstream syncs. Turning them off can't be reviewed, only shows in the settings page, and is the kind of quiet silencing the course counts as small at most.
**Rationale:** These workflows publish upstream's builds and can't run here. The guard is upstream's own pattern, it goes through review in the diff, and a code comment records why.
**Consequences:** Their runs still appear in the Actions tab, marked skipped. If the team ever publishes its own builds, the guard has to come off.

### Decision 2: cutting backend PR time

**Decision:** Refresh the build cache on every push to `main`, run the two unit-test passes as parallel jobs, and move Vitest coverage out of the `test-unit` → `sonarqube` chain. Every database job still runs on every backend PR.
**Alternatives Considered:**
- *Run MySQL, MSSQL and Postgres on a PR only when it touches `models/`, `modules/setting/` or `services/migrations/`.* Rejected because the Postgres-only failures in `TestMilestoneBurndown` (three branches) and `TestRepoCalendar` came from `services/issue` and `routers/`, outside those paths, so they would have reached `main` without any warning.
- *Drop `-race` or the `gogit` pass on PRs.* That would save the most time, but it removes checks without fixing anything, and the course counts that as silencing.
- *Only add more shards.* It uses more runners for the same work, so PRs would start waiting on each other because of the org's limit of 20 jobs at once.
**Rationale:** Most of the extra time goes to compiling and to jobs waiting on each other. Fixing that shortens the run and keeps every check.
**Consequences:** One more job per backend PR. Each unit-test job sets up its own service containers. The 22-minute target is limited by the slowest database job, which is MySQL or MSSQL in most runs.

### Decision 3: how the cache gets refreshed

**Decision:** `cache-seeder` runs on every push to `main`. It saves under `gobuild-<go.sum hash>-<commit sha>` with a `restore-keys` fallback to the newest entry, and warms `-race -cover` as well as `-race`. Update the comment at `.github/actions/go-cache/action.yml:7-8` to give the new reason.
**Alternatives Considered:**
- *Keep the key based only on `go.sum`.* A saved key can't be overwritten, so the cache never updates until `go.sum` changes.
- *Let PR jobs save the cache.* A PR's cache is only visible to that PR and the PRs based on it, so other PRs can't use it, and several jobs writing at once would fight over the same key.
**Rationale:** Caches saved from `main` are visible to every PR, and one key per commit means the newest build is always available.
**Consequences:** Each entry is about 2.25 GB against the repo's 10 GB cache limit, so GitHub keeps about four and evicts the oldest. The `gomod` and `golint` caches share that limit, so eviction can drop them too and slow `lint-backend` and module downloads. One extra seeder run per merge.

### Decision 4: running the suites on `main` and on demand

**Decision:** Let the existing `pull-db-tests.yml` and `pull-e2e-tests.yml` jobs run on `push` to `main`, on `v*-csci435-*` tags and on `workflow_dispatch` (with a `ref` input that checkout uses), by changing each `pull_request`-only condition to `github.event_name != 'pull_request' || <the existing files-changed check>`. Pushes to `main` share one concurrency group with `cancel-in-progress` false, so a running job is never cancelled. Each tag and each manual run gets its own group, so it neither waits on nor replaces a `main` run. Pull request runs keep the group they have now.
**Alternatives Considered:**
- *A new `main-suites.yml` that copies the jobs.* The copies would drift away from the PR jobs.
- *Turn the jobs into one `workflow_call` workflow used by both.* No copies, but it rewrites upstream's files the most, which makes upstream syncs harder.
- *Keep the `files-changed` filter on pushes to `main`, so docs-only merges skip the suites.* Most merges here are docs-only, and the two `db-tests` failures linked under Problem both came after docs-only merges, so repeat runs on an unchanged tree are how a flaky test shows up. Replacing the waiting run caps the cost at one queued run.
**Rationale:** Changing the conditions keeps one definition for each job and touches as few upstream lines as possible. Starting a run by hand with a `ref` input works for old tags, which don't have this workflow file.
**Consequences:** About 9 jobs per merge on `main`. When merges come in bursts, a waiting run is replaced by the newest one, so a failure may cover more than one merge, and the replaced run shows as cancelled on its commit; that saves runner time against the org's limit of 20 jobs. Every suite still `needs: files-changed`, so on push, tag and manual runs that job has to succeed (or be bypassed) even when it has no base to compare against, or every suite is skipped. A manual run takes the workflow file from `main` but `.github/actions/*` and the Makefile from the ref it checks out. `v1.27.3-csci435-s2` has the same actions and make targets as `main`; a ref from before those existed may not run.

## Scope

medium, `scope: medium`. Changes `pull-db-tests.yml`, `pull-e2e-tests.yml`, `pull-compliance.yml` (timeouts), `cache-seeder.yml`, the `go-cache` action and the four release workflows. No product code changes. Evidence needs several pushes to `main`, a tag push, a manual run against a tag and four timed PR runs, each checked against the before numbers.

_**Agent (claude-fable-5-2 2026-11-14 02:57:09Z)**_

Moderately easy, and nothing permanent if you clean up, but I'd skip it: it is close to building the first third of #181 on a throwaway branch.

**Why it's more than a one-line change**

- **The stale key blocks the save.** The seeder's cache key already exists on `main`, and `actions/cache` doesn't save when it finds an exact match. The branch would have to change the key and the restore fallback, which is Decision 3.
- **One job can't fill the cache.** MySQL, Postgres and the unit tests each compile different variants. The seeder itself would have to run on the PR, so `cache-seeder.yml` needs a `pull_request` trigger too.
- **The PR must count as backend.** A change under `.github/` alone only triggers sqlite, so it also needs a token change to a backend file.
- **Time:** about an hour of waiting — the seeder run, then a full `db-tests` run, ideally two or three to average out the runner noise.

**Lasting effects**

- **Cache quota is the one real risk.** The PR's caches add about 3 GB against the 10 GB limit. If that evicts `main`'s build cache, nothing rebuilds it until `go.sum` changes or #181 merges, so every PR gets slower in the meantime. Checking `gh cache list` first and deleting the PR's entries afterwards avoids this.
- **A closed PR stays in the repo's history.** CodeRabbit, Gitar and SonarQube will comment on it. It has no issue or milestone, so label it clearly as an experiment.
- **Nothing on `main` changes,** and CI minutes are free on a public repo.

**Why I'd skip it**

AC7 is already at 22 minutes with margin, and the real PR produces this same measurement as its evidence. The experiment would only tell you a few days early whether 19.8 is accurate. It also sits awkwardly with the rule that the spec review comes before coding.

## Problem

`main`'s CI status means nothing, `main` skips most of the test suites, and backend PRs are slow for a reason we can fix.

### Main is red on every push, so real failures go unnoticed

- `release-nightly-snapcraft` has failed or been cancelled on all 99 of its runs since the fork (78 failed, 21 cancelled, 0 passed). The latest one, [run 43539275792](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/43539275792), stops with `fatal: empty string is not a valid pathspec`. `snap/part-gitea-pull.sh:33` reads the newest tag with `%(tag)`, which is empty for lightweight tags, and all our `v1.27.3-csci435-*` tags are lightweight. Even with annotated tags it would fail at publish, because the repo has no Snap Store credentials and the `gitea` snap name belongs to upstream.
- `release-nightly` has never finished: 98 runs were cancelled and 1 is queued ([example](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/43537000589)). Its jobs need upstream's private `namespace-profile-gitea-release-*` runners. The next push cancels each run, or GitHub drops it after 24 hours in the queue.
- `release-tag-version` matches `v1.*`, so it has run for every sprint tag, and all three runs were cancelled after sitting queued for those runners: s0 ([35251424595](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/35251424595)), s1 ([37872246874](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/37872246874)) and s2 ([40956082407](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/40956082407)). The s3 tag will do the same.
- The noise is hiding a real failure. `db-tests` failed on `main` after two docs-only merges ([43345969430](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/43345969430), [43296442804](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/43296442804)) with the flaky `repo-issue-edit.test.ts` test from #171. Nobody noticed, because every `main` commit was already red.

### Main never runs most of the test suites

Every integration job in `pull-db-tests.yml` has `if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'` (lines 20, 56, 91, 188, 236), and `pull-e2e-tests.yml` runs only on pull requests too. A push to `main` runs `test-unit` and `sonarqube` (Go unit tests and Vitest coverage) and nothing else. Since PRs don't have to be up to date with `main` before merging, two PRs that each pass can break `main` together, and no integration or e2e run would show it. The Sprint 2 tag `v1.27.3-csci435-s2` (`40e0aa79`) has no test runs at all, so D8's Suite health section has no CI baseline to quote.

### Backend PRs take about 28 minutes, mostly compiling and waiting

Full backend `db-tests` runs take 23.3 to 30.1 min, with a median of about 27.6 (e.g. [43524265133](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/43524265133)). Waiting for a runner isn't the cause: the median wait is 2 seconds. The time goes to three things:

- The build cache is stale. `cache-seeder` has run once ([40807939468](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/40807939468), Oct 29), because it only triggers when `go.sum`, `.golangci.yml` or the cache files change. Its `gobuild-<go.sum hash>` key can never be overwritten, so the cache is now 141 commits behind `main`. It also warms the `-race` build but not `-race -cover`. As a result, each `test-unit` pass spends about 3.6 minutes compiling before the first package result, and every other Go test job compiles more than it should too.
- The two unit-test passes run one after the other. `test-unit` runs the normal pass (9.6 to 12.1 min) and then the `gogit` pass (9.4 to 11.5 min).
- `sonarqube` waits on `test-unit`. It has `needs: test-unit` and runs the Vitest coverage itself, so it can't start until both unit passes are done.

## Goal

`main` is green unless one of our own suites failed, it runs the integration and e2e suites after every merge and on every sprint tag, and anyone can run them against any ref. Backend PRs get the same checks as now, every database included, in noticeably less time.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: Given a push to `main`, when CI runs, then `release-nightly` and `release-nightly-snapcraft` show as skipped (not failed, cancelled or queued). Given a pushed `v1.*` tag, `release-tag-version` shows as skipped. `release-tag-rc` only triggers on `v1*-rc*` tags, which the course never pushes, so its guard is checked in the diff. Every job in the four workflows has the skip condition, with a same-line comment citing #181 and saying the workflow only runs upstream.
- [ ] AC2: Given any merge to `main`, docs-only ones included, when CI runs, then sqlite, MySQL, MSSQL and Postgres migration plus integration tests, Go unit tests, Vitest and the Playwright e2e suite all run against the merged commit. A newer merge never cancels a run that has already started. If several merges land while a run is in progress, only the newest waiting run is kept: the suites then run against the newest merged commit, and the replaced run shows as cancelled, never failed.
- [ ] AC3: Given a team member opens Actions → `db-tests` or `e2e-tests` → Run workflow and enters a ref (e.g. `v1.27.3-csci435-s2`), or someone pushes a `v*-csci435-*` tag, when the run finishes, then the suites from AC2 have run against that ref. A tag run or manual run never replaces a `main` run and is never replaced by one.
- [ ] AC4: Given a push to `main`, when CI runs, then the Go build cache is saved again under a key tied to that commit and includes the `-race -cover` build. Given a backend PR branched from `main` after that save, with no Go changes under `modules/` or `models/` (changes there recompile most of the tree whatever the cache holds), when `test-unit`'s normal pass runs, then the first package result appears at most 1 minute after `make test-backend` starts (about 3.6 minutes now).
- [ ] AC5: Given a backend PR, when `db-tests` runs, then the normal and `gogit` unit-test passes run as two separate jobs at the same time. Both run `make test-check`, and only the normal pass uploads Go coverage.
- [ ] AC6: Given any `db-tests` run, when it runs, then Vitest coverage runs in its own job, at the same time as the Go unit tests. `sonarqube` scans both coverage reports, and a failing Vitest test still makes the `db-tests` run fail. `sonarqube` runs only on pull requests and pushes to `main`, and is skipped on tag pushes and manual runs, so an old ref never replaces `main`'s analysis in SonarQube Cloud.
- [ ] AC7: Given the first attempt of four backend PR runs after the fix (a backend PR is one where `files-changed` reports `backend == 'true'`; re-runs don't count), when they finish, then the median wall-clock time of `db-tests` (from the run being created to its last job finishing, runner queue time included) is at most 22 minutes (about 27.6 now), and every job that ran on a backend PR before this change still runs. No database, `-race` or `gogit` coverage is removed.
- [ ] AC8: Given `pull-db-tests.yml`, `pull-e2e-tests.yml` and `pull-compliance.yml`, then every job with steps has a job-level `timeout-minutes` of at most 60, so a hung job stops there instead of at GitHub's 6-hour default. The `files-changed` jobs are exempt: they call a reusable workflow, where GitHub doesn't allow `timeout-minutes`, and its `detect` job already has a 3-minute timeout.

## Out of Scope

- Fixing the flaky `repo-issue-edit.test.ts` test. That's #171. This issue makes sure such a failure turns `main` red where people will see it.
- The Postgres-only failures in `TestMilestoneBurndown/RealLifecycle` ([38276920412](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/38276920412) and two other branches) and `TestRepoCalendar` ([42658314475](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/42658314475)). They need their own bug report.
- Making status checks required, and protecting tags with a ruleset. Both need repo-admin rights. I'll propose them to the TA once AC2 is green, with one combined check job as the required check, because a skipped job counts as passing.
- Writing each suite's pass/fail/skip counts to the job summary, speeding up `lint-backend` (11 to 12 min, runs alongside the tests), and making individual integration tests faster (#37).

## Open Questions

None open. The one question, whether a 20-minute median was the right target for AC7, was settled on 2026-11-13 by measuring existing runs, and AC7 now says 22 minutes.

- **Fresh cache against stale cache.** The two backend PR runs from Oct 29, within a day of the only `cache-seeder` run ([40897202041](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/40897202041), [40897180193](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/40897180193)), took 19.8 and 16.7 min. The 14 successful backend PR runs from Nov 11 to 13 have a median of 28.8 min.
- **Where a database job's time goes.** From the job logs, compiling (`make backend`, the migration test binary and the integration test binary) takes 3.9 to 6.8 min per job with the stale cache and 0.8 to 1.3 min with a fresh one. The tests themselves take 9.4 to 12.3 min either way. With no compile time at all, MySQL and MSSQL still need 16 to 17 min each: about 3 for setup, 1 for migrations and 12 for tests.
- **Projection.** Taking each of the 14 recent runs, replacing its compile time with the fresh-cache figure and splitting the unit passes gives a median of 19.8 min, with 5 of the 14 over 20 and 2 over 22. The slowest job is a database job every time (MySQL 7 runs, MSSQL 5, sqlite 1, Postgres shard 1 once); unit tests plus `sonarqube` finish at 15 to 17.5 min.
- **Why 22 and not 20.** A 20-minute median would pass or fail on runner luck: MySQL alone ranged from 16.5 to 27.2 min on the same cache. Reaching 20 reliably means splitting both MySQL and MSSQL, since they take turns being slowest, which adds two jobs per PR against the org's limit of 20.
- **Limits of the measurement.** Only two fresh-cache runs exist, they predate `-cover`, and the suite has grown from about 720 to 729 integration tests since.

## Evidence of Fix

Broken or missing CI check: links to runs before and after.
- **Before:** the runs linked under Problem, and the backend `db-tests` times (median about 27.6 min) with the compile time from [43524265133](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/43524265133).
- **After:**
  - the first push to `main` after the merge, with release workflows skipped (AC1), every suite run (AC2) and the cache saved (AC4);
  - a manual run against `v1.27.3-csci435-s2` (AC3);
  - four backend PR runs with their times, their median and each job's compile time (AC4 to AC7);
  - the diff showing a job-level `timeout-minutes` on every job in the three files (AC8).

Every After item needs the change on `main`, so the PR's Test Evidence lists them as manual, post-merge checks, and the results go in a comment on this issue. The s3 tag push (`release-tag-version` skipped, suites run) only happens at the D9 release, after this issue closes, so it gets a follow-up comment here and isn't part of the closing evidence.

## Design Decision

### Decision 1: stopping the upstream release workflows

**Decision:** Add `if: github.repository == 'go-gitea/gitea'` to each job in the four release workflows, the same guard upstream already uses in `cron-*.yml` and `giteabot.yml`.
**Alternatives Considered:**
- *Fix the release workflows to work on the fork* (annotated tags, our own runners and store accounts). The team doesn't publish binaries, images or snaps, so this would be work for nothing.
- *Delete the files, or turn them off with `gh workflow disable`.* Deleting conflicts with upstream syncs. Turning them off can't be reviewed, only shows in the settings page, and is the kind of quiet silencing the course counts as small at most.
**Rationale:** These workflows publish upstream's builds and can't run here. The guard is upstream's own pattern, it goes through review in the diff, and a code comment records why.
**Consequences:** Their runs still appear in the Actions tab, marked skipped. If the team ever publishes its own builds, the guard has to come off.

### Decision 2: cutting backend PR time

**Decision:** Refresh the build cache on every push to `main`, run the two unit-test passes as parallel jobs, and move Vitest coverage out of the `test-unit` → `sonarqube` chain. Every database job still runs on every backend PR.
**Alternatives Considered:**
- *Run MySQL, MSSQL and Postgres on a PR only when it touches `models/`, `modules/setting/` or `services/migrations/`.* Rejected because the Postgres-only failures in `TestMilestoneBurndown` (three branches) and `TestRepoCalendar` came from `services/issue` and `routers/`, outside those paths, so they would have reached `main` without any warning.
- *Drop `-race` or the `gogit` pass on PRs.* That would save the most time, but it removes checks without fixing anything, and the course counts that as silencing.
- *Only add more shards.* It uses more runners for the same work, so PRs would start waiting on each other because of the org's limit of 20 jobs at once.
**Rationale:** Most of the extra time goes to compiling and to jobs waiting on each other. Fixing that shortens the run and keeps every check.
**Consequences:** One more job per backend PR. Each unit-test job sets up its own service containers. The 22-minute target is limited by the slowest database job, which is MySQL or MSSQL in most runs.

### Decision 3: how the cache gets refreshed

**Decision:** `cache-seeder` runs on every push to `main`. It saves under `gobuild-<go.sum hash>-<commit sha>` with a `restore-keys` fallback to the newest entry, and warms `-race -cover` as well as `-race`. Update the comment at `.github/actions/go-cache/action.yml:7-8` to give the new reason.
**Alternatives Considered:**
- *Keep the key based only on `go.sum`.* A saved key can't be overwritten, so the cache never updates until `go.sum` changes.
- *Let PR jobs save the cache.* A PR's cache is only visible to that PR and the PRs based on it, so other PRs can't use it, and several jobs writing at once would fight over the same key.
**Rationale:** Caches saved from `main` are visible to every PR, and one key per commit means the newest build is always available.
**Consequences:** Each entry is about 2.25 GB against the repo's 10 GB cache limit, so GitHub keeps about four and evicts the oldest. The `gomod` and `golint` caches share that limit, so eviction can drop them too and slow `lint-backend` and module downloads. One extra seeder run per merge.

### Decision 4: running the suites on `main` and on demand

**Decision:** Let the existing `pull-db-tests.yml` and `pull-e2e-tests.yml` jobs run on `push` to `main`, on `v*-csci435-*` tags and on `workflow_dispatch` (with a `ref` input that checkout uses), by changing each `pull_request`-only condition to `github.event_name != 'pull_request' || <the existing files-changed check>`. Each tag and each manual run gets its own group, so it neither waits on nor replaces a `main` run. Pull request runs keep the group they have now.
**Alternatives Considered:**
- *A new `main-suites.yml` that copies the jobs.* The copies would drift away from the PR jobs.
- *Turn the jobs into one `workflow_call` workflow used by both.* No copies, but it rewrites upstream's files the most, which makes upstream syncs harder.
- *Keep the `files-changed` filter on pushes to `main`, so docs-only merges skip the suites.* Most merges here are docs-only, and the two `db-tests` failures linked under Problem both came after docs-only merges, so repeat runs on an unchanged tree are how a flaky test shows up. Replacing the waiting run caps the cost at one queued run.
**Rationale:** Changing the conditions keeps one definition for each job and touches as few upstream lines as possible. Starting a run by hand with a `ref` input works for old tags, which don't have this workflow file.
**Consequences:** About 9 jobs per merge on `main`. When merges come in bursts, a waiting run is replaced by the newest one, so a failure may cover more than one merge, and the replaced run shows as cancelled on its commit; that saves runner time against the org's limit of 20 jobs.
